skill.name: xcrawl-scrape
skill.description: Use this skill for XCrawl scrape tasks, including single-URL fetch, format selection, sync or async execution, and JSON extraction with prompt or json_schema.
skill.summary: Extract a single web page through XCrawl with selectable formats, structured fields, and synchronous or asynchronous execution.
skill.author: xcrawl-api

security_audit.summary: All 150 static findings describe Markdown syntax, intended API calls, or dedicated configuration access rather than the alleged threats. Two contextual risks remain: disabled target TLS verification by default and unredacted request payloads that can expose supplied credentials. No evidence found of malicious intent, unauthorized credential collection, or embedded prompt injection.

remediation.issue: Target TLS verification is documented as disabled by default.
remediation.suggestion: Set request.skip_tls_verification to false in every example and generated request; require explicit user approval before disabling certificate verification.

remediation.issue: The output contract requires request payloads without redacting sensitive headers, cookies, or webhook credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Require redaction of request.cookies, sensitive request.headers, and webhook.headers before displaying payloads; never include authentication secrets in transcripts.

semantic_findings.title: Target TLS Verification Disabled by Default
semantic_findings.description: The request table documents skip_tls_verification with a true default, while the workflow advises keeping only necessary options. Requests that omit this option can accept invalid target certificates, allowing intercepted content or disclosure of supplied cookies and headers.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The insecure default is explicit in the parameter table, and examples do not override it. Actual provider behavior was not tested.

semantic_findings.title: Output Contract Can Disclose Supplied Credentials
semantic_findings.description: The output contract requires returning the request_payload used for the request without any redaction instruction. Supported payload fields include cookies, request headers, and webhook headers, which can expose session or callback secrets in conversation history.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The contract explicitly requires the used payload, and sensitive input fields are documented. Disclosure depends on the user supplying secret-bearing values.

content.user_title: Extract Web Page Data with XCrawl
content.value_statement: Web pages contain content that is difficult to collect in consistent formats. This skill guides XCrawl requests for page content, structured extraction, and asynchronous result retrieval.
actual_capabilities: Build single-page scrape requests with explicit output formats, including Markdown, HTML, links, screenshots, and structured data.
Run synchronous scrapes or create asynchronous tasks and poll their result endpoint.
Configure structured extraction using a prompt or JSON Schema.
Set documented rendering, device, locale, proxy location, cookie, and header options.
Return upstream response bodies, task identifiers, status, timestamps, and reported credit usage.
limitations: Requires an XCrawl account, available credits, network access, and a provider key in the local configuration file.
Depends on the hosted XCrawl API and local curl or a Node runtime supporting fetch; no standalone scraper is included.
Covers individual page requests, not automatic site discovery or multi-page crawl orchestration.
Documents disabled target TLS verification and unredacted payload output; explicitly enable verification and require secret redaction.

use_cases.title: Collect Page Content for Research
use_cases.description: Retrieve Markdown and links from a public source page, then request a separate summary when needed.

use_cases.title: Extract Product Fields
use_cases.description: Define product fields and accepted null values before requesting structured extraction from a product page.

use_cases.title: Retrieve Rendered Page Evidence
use_cases.description: Request a rendered screenshot with a defined viewport and inspect task status and API errors.

prompt_templates.title: Fetch Page Markdown
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch [public URL] synchronously with XCrawl and return Markdown plus links. Enable target TLS verification and redact secrets from displayed payloads.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: retrieve one page with explicit output formats.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Named Fields
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract title, price, and currency from [product URL]. Allow null for missing values. Enable target TLS verification and redact secrets from displayed payloads.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: define a focused extraction contract.

prompt_templates.title: Capture a Mobile Screenshot
prompt_templates.prompt: Request a mobile screenshot of [public URL] with a 402 by 874 viewport. Enable target TLS verification and redact secrets from displayed payloads.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: configure rendering and screenshot output.

prompt_templates.title: Run Asynchronous Schema Extraction
prompt_templates.prompt: Scrape [public URL] asynchronously using [JSON Schema]. Enable target TLS verification. Poll with a retry limit until completion or failure. Redact secrets from displayed payloads.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine a schema, asynchronous retrieval, and bounded polling.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: fetch a public article as Markdown and links, then summarize the result.
output: Illustrative summary: the synchronous scrape completed with Markdown and links.
The response includes the page title, extracted content, outgoing links, and task metadata.
Actual content and credit usage depend on the upstream response.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: extract product title, price, and currency asynchronously, then summarize task status.
output: Illustrative summary: the task progressed from pending to completed.
The extracted title is Sample Product, the price is 49, and the currency is USD.
These values are examples, not results from a live scrape.

best_practices: Define the authorized URL, required fields, accepted null values, and output formats before making a request.
Set request.skip_tls_verification to false, protect the local key file, and redact sensitive headers and cookies from displayed payloads.
Use bounded asynchronous polling and inspect terminal status, error details, and reported credit usage.
anti_patterns: Sending private URLs, cookies, or authentication headers to the hosted provider without authorization.
Relying on disabled target TLS verification or exposing secrets through raw payload output.
Polling indefinitely or treating extracted fields as verified facts without checking the source.

faq.question: What must I configure before using this skill?
faq.answer: Create ~/.xcrawl/config.json with your XCRAWL_API_KEY and ensure your account has credits. Use curl or a suitable Node runtime.

faq.question: Which output formats are documented?
faq.answer: The documented formats are HTML, raw HTML, Markdown, links, summary, screenshot, and JSON. Availability depends on the upstream API.

faq.question: Can I extract specific fields?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents extraction prompts and JSON Schema options. Define required fields and how missing values should be handled.

faq.question: How does asynchronous scraping work?
faq.answer: Create an asynchronous scrape, capture its task identifier, and poll the result endpoint until completion or failure. Set a polling limit.

faq.question: Does this skill crawl an entire website?
faq.answer: No. It documents single-page scrape requests and result retrieval. Automatic link discovery and full-site crawl management are outside its scope.

faq.question: What security precautions should I take?
faq.answer: Enable target TLS verification, protect the local key file, and redact secrets from displayed payloads. Only submit data you may share with XCrawl.
